t: This is Cavendish Square, a public garden square in Marylebone, with an underground car park beneath it. Wigmore Street, Harley Street, Chandos Street and Cavendish Place all meet at its northern side. Robert Cecil, who became one of the architects of the League of Nations and won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1937, was born here. Among those who died here are General Sir Robert Thomas Wilson, later Governor of Gibraltar, the Earl of Abercorn, who also wrote on magnetism and musical harmony, and the architect Thomas Talbot Bury.
